scenario_narratives.base: The fee franchise (DL Securities Type 1/4/6, DL Family Office, DL Asset Management) grows mid-single digits off the June 2026 retail virtual-asset trading approval and family-office AUM, and its EBITDA margin recovers from roughly break-even (FY2025) to the mid/high teens; the 4.2 EH/s mining fleet is run to the end of its life without replacement, producing a declining revenue stream that is EBITDA-positive for four or five years and then switched off, so the terminal value is the fee business alone at 10x owner FCF. The investment portfolio is carried at the haircuts in equity_bridge: Level-3 marks on the chairman's Carmel land project and the NeuralFin associate are halved or worse, everything else is lightly discounted. The convertible bond is repaid in cash in December 2027 from the HK$370m cash pile.
scenario_narratives.bull: BTC rallies and the fleet earns 35-40% EBITDA margins for several years with some reinvestment, retail virtual-asset trading and RWA tokenisation (DL Tower LPF, Animoca Brands LPF, ONE Carmel) turn DL Securities into a fee platform growing 10%, margins reach the low twenties, and the terminal multiple expands to 12x at an 11% rate. The investment portfolio is still carried at the base haircuts, so this scenario does NOT give credit for the Level-3 marks being right; if Carmel and NeuralFin are worth book, nav_memo adds c.HK$0.29/share on top.
scenario_narratives.bear: BTC falls to where hosted mining is uneconomic, the fleet is switched off within three years and written off, the fee businesses stay at FY2025's break-even-to-10% EBITDA margin with no growth, lease and corporate costs absorb most of the segment profit, and the operating business is worth roughly nothing at 13% and 8x. Intrinsic value is then the haircut bridge less net debt. What this scenario does NOT model -- and the 40% weight partly stands in for -- is the Level-3 portfolio being marked down: with Carmel, NeuralFin and the L3 funds at zero and the rest at 70%, the bridge alone is HK$0.30/share (nav_memo.bridge_severe_per_share).

valuation_philosophy.summary: DL Holdings is a controlled Hong Kong financial holdco whose value sits on the balance sheet, not in the P&L: six operating segments earned HK$0.3m of segment profit in FY2026 and the group's EBIT excluding fair-value gains was about -HK$20m, while HK$1.57bn of placings at HK$2.95-3.05 funded a mining fleet, a BTC/gold-token treasury, fund and land investments and a self-marked AI associate. The valuation is therefore a sum of parts: owner-FCF on the fee businesses plus a run-off of the mining fleet, and a haircut NAV of the investment portfolio. At HK$0.83 the stock trades at 0.63x stated NAV (HK$1.31) and at the at-book bridge value (HK$0.81) before any operating value; the question is entirely whether the Level-3 marks (HK$727m, 27% of equity) are real. We assume roughly half are not.
key_risks_to_valuation: Level-3 marks: Carmel Reserve (HK$322m, related party, residual-method land valuation) and NeuralFin (HK$340m, DCF at 120-300% user growth) are 25% of equity and 100%+ of FY2026 profit; a write-down to cost removes c.HK$0.29/share of stated NAV.

Bitcoin price and mining difficulty: the HK$617m fleet is valued only through its run-off cash flows; at a BTC price below hosted-mining cash cost it is worth nothing and the digital-asset treasury (HK$146m) falls with it.

Governance and related-party flows: controlling shareholder Mr Chen sold and re-subscribed 456m shares in two top-up placings, the fleet vendor/placee/CB holder Evergreen Wealth, HK$34.5m due from related parties, HK$68m of unpaid disposal consideration, and a HK$180m guarantee to a fund the group manages.

Dilution overhang: 53.8m CB shares at HK$3.17, 40m warrants at HK$3.80 and 13.4m earn-out shares are out of the money today but a recovery toward HK$3 would bring 107m shares (5%) back; the trustee holds c.70m shares for staff awards.

Liquidity: the US$21.85m (HK$170m) zero-coupon CB is a cash repayment on 30 Dec 2027; the March 2026 resolution to redirect placing proceeds to power sites, AI data centres and GPUs could consume the HK$370m cash pile before then.

Fee-business economics: FY2025 EBITDA after corporate cost was roughly zero; the margin recovery in the base case rests on the retail virtual-asset licence and family-office growth that have not yet shown up in segment profit (licensed-business segment profit fell to HK$18.1m from HK$25.3m).

inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD flows. HK 10-year government yield c.3.5% + 6% ERP x beta c.1.4 for a controlled HK financial micro-cap with crypto-mining and Level-3 exposure = c.12% cost of equity; the group is >85% equity-funded so WACC ~ CoE = 12%. Risk is charged ONCE: the same 12% is used in all three scenarios and the business-specific risk (marks, BTC, governance) lives in the driver paths and the 40/45/15 probability weights, not in a stacked premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: full FY2026 lease cash (principal 10.3 + interest 1.6 = HK$11.9m, c.HK$12m held flat) charged via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities excluded from total_debt; da_pct_path excludes right-of-use depreciation.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI (HK$34.4m book) and the third-party investors' share of a consolidated structured entity (other financial liabilities HK$10.6m) are deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: holdco sum-of-parts on the engine route, NOT a plain owner-FCF DCF and NOT earnings-at-CoE. Routing: FY2026 'profit' of HK$363m is HK$397m of other gains -- HK$241.9m Level-3 mark-up of the 34.3% NeuralFin associate (reclassified from equity accounting at a deemed cost of HK$98m to FVTPL at the US$127m post-money of a US$5m round) and HK$117.5m of Level-3 gains on the related-party Carmel Reserve LLC land project -- while the six operating segments earned HK$0.3m of segment profit in aggregate and the group's EBIT ex-gains was c.-HK$20m. Capitalising those earnings at a cost of equity would capitalise valuer marks; a plain FCF DCF would value a HK$1.57bn investment portfolio at zero. So: (1) the fee businesses (licensed brokerage/advisory HK$119.7m, family office HK$56.8m, enterprise solutions HK$10.9m, apparel HK$4.5m) plus the bitcoin-mining fleet (9,695 machines, 4.23 EH/s, HK$617m book) run through the owner-FCF engine, with mining modelled in HARVEST mode (revenue declining to zero by year 10 as difficulty rises and the fleet ages, maintenance-only capex, fleet fully depreciated by year 4) so the terminal value is the fee business alone; (2) every financial asset goes into equity_bridge at a haircut that reflects its fair-value level and counterparty (listed 80%, Level-2 funds 85%, Level-3 Carmel/NeuralFin/other 40-50%, BTC/XAUT 85% for post-balance-date volatility, loan book 85%, margin book 90%, unpaid disposal consideration and related-party receivables 50%); (3) goodwill (226.4), intangibles (79.0), right-of-use assets and operating working capital are excluded -- the fee businesses are valued on their flows. Money-lending revenue and margin interest are stripped from the flows because their source assets sit in the bridge (matching-asset rule). SBC-near-zero market: house and street coincide, band_position is reported but degenerate. LIMITATION: the bridge is scenario-invariant on the engine route, so the bear scenario does NOT capture a write-down of the Level-3 marks; nav_memo gives the at-book / haircut / severe NAV per share, and the bear probability weight (40%) is set high partly to carry that tail. Price fell from HK$3.43 (52-week high) to HK$0.83; the FY2026 placings were done at HK$2.95-3.05, so the market now prices the company at c.0.62x stated NAV of HK$1.31/share (post-bonus, ex-dividend).
inputs.post_balance_date_items_not_modelled: June 2026: ARTi Pre-A round at US$30m pre-money (group holds 47.62%; implied stake c.HK$130m, not on the 31 Mar 2026 balance sheet at that value); US$5m subscription to ONE Carmel Lot A LPF (8% fixed + 20% excess profit); April 2026 US$10m Cango Inc convertible notes (cash moved into an investment, value-neutral at cost); 24 June 2026 SFC approval for DL Securities to offer retail virtual-asset trading. None is included in the bridge; ARTi is the only one that is an unrecorded asset and it is left as upside. The proposed special dividend by way of distribution in specie of RWA tokens (indicative HK$100m of tokenised LPF interests, structure and timetable not finalised) would move value from the bridge to shareholders' hands and is per-share neutral; it is not modelled.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 10x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 40% (house default 15%): reported profit is >100% Level-3 fair-value marks, the largest single mark is a related-party land project controlled by the chairman, the second largest is a 34.3% associate marked to a US$5m financing round, the money-lending book is 88% unsecured, HK$68m of disposal consideration has been outstanding for two year-ends, and the mining fleet was bought from a party (Evergreen Wealth) that is also a placee and convertible-bond holder; the engine bear cannot write the marks down, so the weight carries that tail. Bull 15%: needs BTC, retail VA trading and RWA tokenisation to all work. Base 45%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
